RagShortTexts: Castile's push toward Cádiz and Jerez ignited covert Mudéjar coordination backed by Granada.

Variants.Content: Around 1259, Alfonso X of Castile pursued aggressive expansion toward the Atlantic coast, aiming to secure Cádiz and placing Jerez under protectorate garrisoning. Fearing total encirclement, Muhammad I of Granada covertly supplied arms and messages to Mudéjar populations under Castilian rule, sparking coordinated rebellion.
Securing Cádiz delivers an Atlantic naval haven commanding the Straits of Gibraltar. Yet in Jerez, nominally compliant Mudéjar townsmen await the Sultan's signal to expel the royal garrison.
Moorish smiths keep bellows pumping through the night, converting pruning hooks into spearpoints. Heavy Castilian tithes on olive presses have pushed common folk past breaking point.
